private_note: I get one draw for a generation, so I weigh losses more than gains. Alder has the same average as today but raises the floor from 22 to 32 and costs the top only about 4 percent. Cedar has the highest average, but a one-in-five chance of 15 with no coverage is too steep. Hazel and Birch cut the average by a fifth. On a log-utility check: Alder, then Today, then Cedar, Hazel, Birch.
statement: Fellow delegates, each of us gets one draw, and we live with it for a generation. I am asking which plan protects me without throwing away what we have. Alder does that. Its average income is the same as today's, the lowest fifth goes from 22 to 32 with guaranteed health coverage, and the top fifth gives up only 10 of its 252. Cedar promises more on average, but one in five of us would live on 15 with no safety net, and I won't stake my household on that. Hazel and Birch raise the floor further, but they shrink the whole economy by a fifth, so four in five of us would end up with less. We need nine votes, and failure just leaves us with today. Alder beats today for nearly everyone. I urge you to make it our common ground.
